region: Georgia and Armenia (Tbilisi, Kazbegi, Kakheti, Debed canyon, Dilijan, Lake Sevan, Yerevan)
title: Caucasus — Supra, Qvevri and Monasteries Between Two Capitals
subtitle: Tbilisi to Yerevan in thirteen days: Kazbegi in snow, Kakheti wine cellars and cliff-carved monasteries
summary: A thirteen-day open-jaw route from Tbilisi to Yerevan: Georgian Orthodox heritage, Kazbegi snowshoeing, qvevri winemaking and Armenian UNESCO monasteries. Route avoids Syunik and the Azerbaijan border zone.
introduction: Tbilisi's sulphur baths and wooden balconies start the route, then a driver takes the group over the Jvari Pass to Stepantsminda for a snowshoe climb to Gergeti Trinity Church under Mount Kazbek. In Kakheti, guesthouse families open their qvevri cellars and host supra dinners with toasts and home-made wine. A walk across the Sadakhlo border leads into the Debed canyon's UNESCO monasteries, forests above Dilijan, Lake Sevan at 1,900 m and pink Yerevan, ending with Garni and Geghard. The route deliberately avoids Svaneti, Tusheti and Armenia's Syunik province, which are winter-inaccessible or officially advised against.

exceptional.vsOman: Oman is desert, wadis and camping with a rented 4x4; this trip is mountains, snow, monasteries and family guesthouses, travelled with local drivers because winter roads and the border make self-drive impractical.
exceptional.vsPackageTourism: Package tours follow summer Tbilisi-Kazbegi-Yerevan bus loops; here the group sleeps with Kakheti winemaking families, climbs Gergeti in winter conditions and crosses the border on foot, in the quiet season.
exceptional.vsPortfolio: No other destination in the portfolio combines two ancient Christian nations, a supra and qvevri wine culture recognised by UNESCO and a winter mountain church ascent on a single compact route.

duration.note: Includes outbound flight on day 1 and return flight on day 13; open-jaw Tbilisi-Yerevan

recommendedTravelWindow.rationale: March is warmer, the Jvari Pass clears gradually and Kazbegi is still snow-covered; early March keeps Gergeti on snowshoes. February has higher pass-closure risk.

februarySuitability.summary: Cold, with frequent Jvari Pass closures and deep snow at Kazbegi; low season prices and quiet cellars. Mountain days likely disrupted.

marchSuitability.summary: Still wintry at altitude but milder in Tbilisi, Kakheti and Yerevan; pass closure risk is medium and Gergeti is walkable with snowshoes or boots.

march.notes: Tbilisi ≈ 11 °C; Yerevan ≈ 10 °C; Kazbegi ≈ 2 °C with snow still lying.

climate.snowAndMountainAccess: Jvari Pass (Military Highway) can close several times a month Nov-March, usually for hours, sometimes days. Svaneti/Ushguli and Tusheti are not used in winter; Tusheti's road is closed in winter.

climate.airQuality: Tbilisi and Yerevan can have winter air pollution; not quantified here.
climate.wildlifeSeasonality: Brown bears hibernate in the mountains; not a focus.

geography.summary: The route runs from Tbilisi along the south slope of the Greater Caucasus, through the Alazani wine valley and the Debed canyon to Armenia's volcanic highlands and Lake Sevan.
geography.distinctive: A single 13-day line that crosses the Greater Caucasus (Jvari Pass), a river valley wine region, a forested canyon and the largest high-altitude lake in the region.

landscapes.name: Kazbegi and the Terek valley
landscapes.description: Glaciated peaks around Mount Kazbek, with the Gergeti ridge above Stepantsminda.

landscapes.name: Alazani valley
landscapes.description: Vineyards and villages below the Caucasus ridge.

landscapes.name: Lake Sevan
landscapes.description: High-altitude freshwater lake at about 1,900 m.

culture.summary: The oldest Christian states, with Georgian Orthodox and Armenian Apostolic churches, supra feasting and qvevri winemaking, and Soviet and medieval layers in two capitals.

culturalHighlights.name: Qvevri wine and supra, Kakheti
culturalHighlights.description: UNESCO-recognised clay-vessel winemaking and the toastmaster-led feast, experienced in family guesthouses.

culturalHighlights.name: Geghard Monastery and Garni Temple
culturalHighlights.description: Cliff-carved monastery and a Hellenistic temple in the Azat gorge.

culturalHighlights.name: Uplistsikhe
culturalHighlights.description: Rock-cut city of the Iron Age to the Middle Ages.

adventureHighlights.name: Gergeti Trinity Church on snowshoes
adventureHighlights.description: Guided winter ascent of about 400-500 m above Stepantsminda.

adventureHighlights.name: Dilijan National Park walk to Haghartsin
adventureHighlights.description: Low-altitude forest path, snow-free in March in most years.

signatureExperiences.title: Gergeti Trinity Church under Mount Kazbek
signatureExperiences.description: A guided snowshoe or boot walk from Stepantsminda to the 14th-century church.
signatureExperiences.whyDistinctive: The iconic Georgian mountain church seen in winter conditions with almost no other visitors.
signatureExperiences.howToOrganise: Book a local guide through the guesthouse for one day; buffer day built in. Snowshoes can be rented in town.
signatureExperiences.costNote: Guide €90 split four ways plus rental, estimate

signatureExperiences.title: A qvevri cellar and a supra in Kakheti
signatureExperiences.description: A visit to a family marani where wine is made in buried clay vessels, followed by a toasted dinner.
signatureExperiences.whyDistinctive: The oldest continuous winemaking tradition, experienced in a family home, not a tasting room.
signatureExperiences.howToOrganise: Book guesthouses with their own marani; arrange via the guesthouse or a local winemaker.

signatureExperiences.title: Walking across the Georgia-Armenia border to the Debed monasteries
signatureExperiences.description: Crossing at Sadakhlo-Bagratashen on foot, then Haghpat and Sanahin.
signatureExperiences.whyDistinctive: An overland border crossing between two historic nations, followed by UNESCO monasteries in a forested canyon.
signatureExperiences.howToOrganise: Driver to the border, walk across with passports, pre-arranged Armenian driver on the other side.

signatureExperiences.title: Tbilisi sulphur baths and old town
signatureExperiences.description: A private bath room in Abanotubani and an evening in the old town.
signatureExperiences.whyDistinctive: Natural sulphur springs in domed brick baths in a city centre.
signatureExperiences.howToOrganise: Book a private room walk-in; about €12-20 per person.

travelStyle.summary: Hired drivers and a foot border crossing, with a winter guide for Gergeti, guesthouses throughout.

transport.summary: Private drivers (minivan) in Georgia and Armenia, with marshrutkas as the economical alternative; the border is crossed on foot.

modes.description: €70-120 per day in Georgia and €60-100 in Armenia, estimated.
Minibuses from Didube station to Stepantsminda and Kakheti; cheap but slow and schedule-dependent.
Bolt and Yandex in Tbilisi and Yerevan; FCDO advises booking by app.
Sadakhlo to Bagratashen with a taxi on each side.

transport.carRental: Self-drive is not recommended in winter: mountain roads, chains and 4WD for Jvari Pass, cross-border rental restrictions (not verified). Prices for rental were not collected.

drivingRequirements.summary: Winter mountain roads and cross-border rental limits make hired drivers the recommended option.
drivingRequirements.internationalDrivingPermit: UK FCDO says a 1968 IDP is required in Armenia alongside a UK licence; Georgia requirements were not confirmed. Conditional on the licence country.
drivingRequirements.licenceNotes: Two of the four hold car licences; none may ride a motorcycle or scooter without the legal licence.
drivingRequirements.motorcycleNotes: Not needed: marshrutkas, taxis and hired drivers cover all legs.
drivingRequirements.recommendedApproach: Hired driver for each country, marshrutka for the economical variant. Do not drive the Jvari Pass in winter without chains or 4WD.

accommodation.summary: Guesthouses and small hotels with twin rooms; family guesthouses in Stepantsminda, Kakheti and Alaverdi.

camping.summary: Winter temperatures and snow make camping inappropriate.

physicalDifficulty.label: moderate
physicalDifficulty.summary: Mostly easy walking; the Gergeti ascent is the only demanding day and weather may cancel it.

itinerary.summary: Thirteen days: three nights Tbilisi, two Kazbegi, one back in Tbilisi, two in Kakheti, then Alaverdi, Dilijan and two nights in Yerevan.

stops.name: Tbilisi International Airport
stops.description: Arrival airport. Direct Paris-Tbilisi service is reported by flight aggregators but was not verified for 2027 schedules.
stops.transport: Pre-booked transfer or Bolt/Yandex taxi, about 25 min to the old town
stops.accommodation: Guesthouse in Sololaki or Old Tbilisi

stops.name: Tbilisi old town and Abanotubani
stops.description: Two-and-a-half days across three nights: Narikala, sulphur baths, Dry Bridge market, Meidan bazaar, bakeries and cellar restaurants.
stops.culturalImportance: Capital since the 5th century, a crossroads of Persian, Ottoman, Russian and Georgian traditions.
stops.geography: Valley of the Mtkvari river with warm sulphur springs.
stops.accommodation: Guesthouses and small hotels in Sololaki

stops.name: Mtskheta (Svetitskhoveli and Jvari)
stops.description: UNESCO-listed old capital at the confluence of the Aragvi and Mtkvari rivers, 20 km from Tbilisi.
stops.culturalImportance: Seat of the Georgian Church since the 4th century; the cathedral is central to Georgian Orthodox identity.
stops.geography: River confluence below a hilltop monastery.
stops.transport: Driver or marshrutka from Didube, 30 min

stops.name: Uplistsikhe cave town
stops.description: Rock-cut town on a sandstone terrace above the Mtkvari, about 1.5 h from Tbilisi.
activities: Walk the cave streets and halls
stops.culturalImportance: Occupied from the early Iron Age; a pagan and later Christian centre on the Silk Road.

stops.name: Stepantsminda (Kazbegi)
stops.description: Mountain town at 1,740 m under Mount Kazbek, reached by the Georgian Military Highway over the Jvari Pass (2,379 m).
stops.culturalImportance: Highland Khevi community, Orthodox shrines and tower houses.
stops.geography: Greater Caucasus, glaciated peaks above the Terek valley.
stops.transport: Marshrutka or driver, about 3 h each way, pass can close for hours to days

stops.name: Gergeti Trinity Church
stops.description: 14th-century church at about 2,170 m above Stepantsminda; winter ascent on foot, snow permitting.
stops.geography: Ridge below Kazbek with winter snow cover.
stops.transport: On foot, 1.5-3 h ascent depending on snow; 4x4 shuttle only if the road is cleared

stops.name: Telavi and the Alazani valley
stops.description: Kakheti's main town, base for qvevri cellars, Alaverdi and Gremi.
stops.culturalImportance: Heart of Georgian wine culture, with UNESCO-listed qvevri winemaking.
stops.geography: Alazani valley below the Caucasus ridge.
stops.transport: Driver from Tbilisi, 90 km, about 2 h over the Gombori pass

stops.name: Alaverdi Monastery
stops.description: 11th-century cathedral and a monastery cellar still making wine in qvevri.
stops.culturalImportance: One of the tallest medieval churches in Georgia.
stops.geography: Alazani plain with the Caucasus beyond.

stops.name: Sighnaghi
stops.description: Walled hill town above the Alazani valley, with guesthouse dinners and a town wall walk.
stops.culturalImportance: Reconstructed town of the 18th century, known for wine hospitality.
stops.geography: Ridge overlooking the Alazani valley and the Caucasus.

stops.name: Sadakhlo-Bagratashen border crossing
stops.description: Main road crossing between Georgia and Armenia, on the Debed road to Alaverdi; avoids the restricted Ijevan-Noyemberyan road.
activities: Walk across with passports and baggage
stops.transport: Taxi on each side; no vehicle crossing planned with a rental

stops.name: Haghpat and Sanahin monasteries (Alaverdi)
stops.description: UNESCO-listed 10th-13th century monasteries in the Debed canyon, overnight in Alaverdi.
stops.culturalImportance: Centres of medieval Armenian learning and architecture.
stops.transport: Driver, about 70 km from the border

stops.name: Dilijan and Haghartsin Monastery
stops.description: Forest town in Dilijan National Park with the Haghartsin Monastery.
stops.culturalImportance: Spa-town atmosphere and a craft quarter.
stops.geography: Beech and oak forest at 1,200-1,500 m.

stops.name: Lake Sevan and Sevanavank
stops.description: High lake at about 1,900 m with a 9th-century monastery on the former island.
stops.culturalImportance: Settled since the Bronze Age; centre of Armenian monastic tradition.
stops.geography: One of the largest high-altitude lakes in the world.
stops.transport: Driver on the north-west shore, about 40 km from Dilijan

stops.name: Yerevan
stops.description: Capital of rose-pink tuff buildings, the Cascade, Vernissage market and brandy cellars.
activities: Cascade and views of Mount Ararat
stops.culturalImportance: One of the oldest continually inhabited cities; the Soviet-era plan frames the Mother Armenia monument.
stops.geography: Ararat plain, Mount Ararat on the horizon.

stops.name: Garni Temple and Geghard Monastery
stops.description: Greco-Roman temple and a cliff-carved monastery, 30-40 min east of Yerevan in the Azat gorge.
stops.culturalImportance: UNESCO-listed Geghard; Garni is the only standing Hellenistic temple in Armenia.
stops.geography: Basalt gorge of the Azat river.

stops.name: Zvartnots International Airport (Yerevan)
stops.description: Departure airport, 20 min from the city centre.
